findings.title: Zero flusher processes possible causes crash / silent data loss
findings.body: self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) with no validation. If --flusher-processes 0 (or negative) is passed, num_processes becomes 0, then `i % self.num_processes` raises ZeroDivisionError, or if there are zero shards no processes are created and segments are never flushed. The CLI option defaults to 1 but accepts any int. This can crash the consumer on startup or silently drop all segments.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag shards vs shard
findings.body: Produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} but wait_produce uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. The plural key splits the metric series, breaking dashboards/alerts that filter on shard and hiding flusher latency after the multiprocess change.

findings.title: Restart leaks thread/process and double-flushes shards
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive only kills when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). In test/thread mode (produce_to_pipe set) and for hung threads, _create_process_for_shards overwrites self.processes/process entry without stopping the old thread. Two threads then run SpanFlusher.main on the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and races in flush_segments/done_flush_segments. The unused _create_process_for_shard helper has the same leak.

findings.title: join() ignores timeout and terminates healthy processes
findings.body: join() computes remaining_time but never uses it, polls with `while process.is_alive() and deadline > time.time()`, then unconditionally calls process.terminate() even if the process already exited, and `break`s out of the loop on deadline leaving remaining processes never waited on or terminated. Shutdown/rebalance can hang, leak processes, or SIGTERM a cleanly-exited flusher.

findings.title: Flaky sync after mocking time.sleep to no-op
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None for aggressive flushing, then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting to give flusher threads time to process after drift change. The mocked sleep does nothing, so there is no synchronization with the background flusher thread; the test relies on a race and can flake. The new test_flusher_processes_limit also only asserts process counts and never verifies segments from shared shards are actually flushed.
